name: Rwanda

findings.local_actor: Government of Rwanda (Ministry of ICT and Innovation; Ministry of Health)
findings.summary: Rwanda and Anthropic signed a three-year non-binding MOU covering health goals (cervical cancer, malaria, maternal mortality), Claude and Claude Code access with API credits for government developers, and formalising an earlier educator and AI-literacy programme.

sources.publisher: Rwanda Ministry of ICT and Innovation

findings.analyst_inference: Used through Anthropic's own service/API, so us pole; base_model given as the Claude family because no specific model version is named. Tier 1: non-binding MOU, no value. Anthropic's post is the counterparty's own announcement, coded S1 as a company release. No hosting or data-residency detail in any source.

findings.summary: Airtel picked Ericsson, rather than Nokia Siemens, to manage its new Rwandan network end-to-end, including OSS/BSS and managed services, as Airtel pledged about US$100m investment over three years.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so third pole. Contract value undisclosed; the US$100m is Airtel's investment pledge, not the contract, so not recorded as a value. RAN/core split not stated. Airtel Rwanda later merged with Tigo Rwanda; current vendor arrangement not checked. Pre-2020 finding.

findings.summary: MTN Rwanda deployed Ericsson multi-band, multi-sector energy-efficient radios to expand and modernise its Kigali network, adding coverage and capacity and making it 5G-ready.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so third pole. Tier 5 because the source describes the radios as deployed; site count and value not given. Scale subnational (Kigali). MTN Rwanda's vendors outside Kigali and for its core were not established.

findings.local_actor: KT Rwanda Networks (KTRN; Government of Rwanda 49%)
findings.summary: Under a 2013 joint venture, Korea Telecom (51%) and Rwanda's government (49%) formed KTRN, which built and runs the national wholesale 4G LTE network with access to national fibre; KT was expected to invest about US$140m.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third (Korean) on the basis that KT, as majority owner and operator, controls the network; the RAN/core equipment vendor was not identified in any opened source, so under the v0.2 equipment-vendor rule the pole could differ. Date is year of JV only. US$140m is an expected investment, recorded as announced.

findings.local_actor: Rwanda Utilities Regulatory Authority (RURA); KT Rwanda Networks
findings.summary: RURA moved to end KTRN's 25-year exclusive right to wholesale 4G, to remove regulatory barriers under the national broadband policy and open 4G to rival operators; compensation was negotiated and a Korean firm later filed an arbitration claim.
findings.analyst_inference: Reversal of exclusivity only: KTRN may keep selling wholesale 4G non-exclusively. Coded regulatory (market liberalisation), not geopolitical, so it should not move the map. The GAR article does not name the claimant in its text (tagged KT) or the forum; outcome unknown.

findings.summary: During talks between President Kagame and Huawei's chairwoman, Huawei signed an MOU with Rwanda's government to help build regional data centres, national broadband, smart grid and smart-education infrastructure; no value was stated.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded S4: the article quotes Huawei and credits photos to Huawei, suggesting company-supplied material. Layer set to networks as broadband is the main named scope; the MOU also touches facilities and power. Tier 1, pre-2020; no evidence found of what, if anything, was delivered under it.

findings.summary: Africa Data Centres, a Cassava Technologies unit, announced a purpose-built 2MW data centre in Kigali, its first in Rwanda, with groundbreaking planned for the first quarter of 2023.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: Cassava is a pan-African group founded by Zimbabwean Strive Masiyiwa (analyst inference on home jurisdiction; not stated in source). Tier 1 announcement; whether construction started or the site operates was not confirmed. A DFC loan to ADC is mentioned but not tied to Kigali, so financier left null.

silicon.null_reason: one dedicated search found no accelerator purchases or deployments in Rwanda; Cassava/Nvidia AI-factory reporting lists South Africa, Egypt, Kenya, Morocco and Nigeria, not Rwanda

applications.null_reason: one search found a 2018 plan to spend Rwf5bn on Kigali public CCTV but no named vendor; no safe-city or surveillance supplier identified

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced in other searches

research_gaps: Which vendor supplied KTRN's 4G LTE RAN and core, and what is the outcome of the 2026 Korean arbitration claim over the revoked exclusivity?

Huawei's actual installed footprint in Rwanda (e.g. a reported 2008 US$35m Rwandatel deal, MTN/Airtel legacy RAN or core, national fibre backbone) — only headlines or company-supplied material surfaced.
Who supplied the Kigali public CCTV system funded in 2018 (Rwf5bn), and is it AI/analytics-enabled?
Did Africa Data Centres' Kigali facility break ground or open? Ownership and builder of the AOS-operated National Data Centre (reported JV with Korea Telecom).
Any concrete Claude deployments (systems, volumes, hosting) under the Anthropic MOU, and any other government AI model adoptions (e.g. Rwanda's AI scaling hub).
